Title: CLI Reference | Plandex Docs

URL Source: https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference

Markdown Content:
All Plandex CLI commands and their options.

Usage[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#usage "Direct link to Usage")
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```
plandex [command] [flags]pdx [command] [flags] # 'pdx' is an alias for 'plandex'
```

Help[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#help "Direct link to Help")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

Built-in help.

```
plandex helppdx h # alias
```

`--all/-a`: List all commands.

For help on a specific command, use:

Plans[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#plans "Direct link to Plans")
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

### new[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#new "Direct link to new")

Start a new plan.

```
plandex newplandex new -n new-plan # with name
```

`--name/-n`: Name of the new plan. The name is generated automatically after first prompt if no name is specified on creation.

### plans[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#plans-1 "Direct link to plans")

List plans. Output includes index, when each plan was last updated, the current branch of each plan, the number of tokens in context, and the number of tokens in the conversation (prior to summarization).

Includes full details on plans in current directory. Also includes names of plans in parent directories and child directories.

```
plandex plansplandex plans --archived # list archived plans onlypdx pl # alias
```

`--archived/-a`: List archived plans only.

### current[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#current "Direct link to current")

Show current plan. Output includes when the plan was last updated and created, the current branch, the number of tokens in context, and the number of tokens in the conversation (prior to summarization).

```
plandex currentpdx cu # alias
```

### cd[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#cd "Direct link to cd")

Set current plan by name or index.

```
plandex cd # select from a list of plansplandex cd some-plan # by nameplandex cd 4 # by index in `plandex plans`
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of plans to select from.

With one argument, Plandex selects a plan by name or by index in the `plandex plans` list.

### delete-plan[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#delete-plan "Direct link to delete-plan")

Delete a plan by name or index.

```
plandex delete-plan # select from a list of plansplandex delete-plan some-plan # by nameplandex delete-plan 4 # by index in `plandex plans`pdx dp # alias
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of plans to select from.

With one argument, Plandex deletes a plan by name or by index in the `plandex plans` list.

### rename[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#rename "Direct link to rename")

Rename the current plan.

```
plandex rename # prompt for new nameplandex rename new-name # set new name
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you for a new name.

With one argument, Plandex sets the new name.

### archive[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#archive "Direct link to archive")

Archive a plan.

```
plandex archive # select from a list of plansplandex archive some-plan # by nameplandex archive 4 # by index in `plandex plans`pdx arc # alias
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of plans to select from.

With one argument, Plandex archives a plan by name or by index in the `plandex plans` list.

### unarchive[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#unarchive "Direct link to unarchive")

Unarchive a plan.

```
plandex unarchive # select from a list of archived plansplandex unarchive some-plan # by nameplandex unarchive 4 # by index in `plandex plans --archived`pdx unarc # alias
```

Context[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#context "Direct link to Context")
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### load[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#load "Direct link to load")

Load files, directories, directory layouts, URLs, notes, images, or piped data into context.

```
plandex load component.ts # single fileplandex load component.ts action.ts reducer.ts # multiple filesplandex load lib -r # loads lib and all its subdirectoriesplandex load tests/**/*.ts # loads all .ts files in tests and its subdirectoriesplandex load . --tree # loads the layout of the current directory and its subdirectories (file names only)plandex load https://redux.js.org/usage/writing-tests # loads the text-only content of the urlnpm test | plandex load # loads the output of `npm test`plandex load -n 'add logging statements to all the code you generate.' # load a note into contextplandex load ui-mockup.png # load an image into contextpdx l component.ts # alias
```

`--recursive/-r`: Load an entire directory and all its subdirectories.

`--tree`: Load directory tree layout with file names only.

`--note/-n`: Load a note into context.

`--force/-f`: Load files even when ignored by .gitignore or .plandexignore.

`--detail/-d`: Image detail level when loading an image (high or low)—default is high. See [https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/vision/low-or-high-fidelity-image-understanding](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/vision/low-or-high-fidelity-image-understanding) for more info.

### ls[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#ls "Direct link to ls")

List everything in the current plan's context. Output includes index, name, type, token size, when the context added, and when the context was last updated.

```
plandex lsplandex list-context # longer alias
```

### rm[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#rm "Direct link to rm")

Remove context by index, range, name, or glob.

```
plandex rm some-file.ts # by nameplandex rm app/**/*.ts # by glob patternplandex rm 4 # by index in `plandex ls`plandx rm 2-4 # by range of indicesplandex remove # longer aliasplandex unload # longer alias
```

### update[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#update "Direct link to update")

Update any outdated context.

```
plandex updatepdx u # alias
```

### clear[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#clear "Direct link to clear")

Remove all context.

Control[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#control "Direct link to Control")
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### tell[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#tell "Direct link to tell")

Describe a task, ask a question, or chat.

```
plandex tell -f prompt.txt # from fileplandex tell # open vim to write promptplandex tell "add a cancel button to the left of the submit button" # inlinepdx t # alias
```

`--file/-f`: File path containing prompt.

`--stop/-s`: Stop after a single model response (don't auto-continue).

`--no-build/-n`: Don't build proposed changes into pending file updates.

`--bg`: Run task in the background.

### continue[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#continue "Direct link to continue")

Continue the plan.

```
plandex continuepdx c # alias
```

`--stop/-s`: Stop after a single model response (don't auto-continue).

`--no-build/-n`: Don't build proposed changes into pending file updates.

`--bg`: Run task in the background.

### build[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#build "Direct link to build")

Build any unbuilt pending changes from the plan conversation.

```
plandex buildpdx b # alias
```

`--bg`: Build in the background.

Changes[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#changes "Direct link to Changes")
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### diff[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#diff "Direct link to diff")

Review pending changes in 'git diff' format.

### changes[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#changes-1 "Direct link to changes")

Review pending changes in a TUI.

### apply[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#apply "Direct link to apply")

Apply pending changes to project files.

```
plandex applypdx ap # alias
```

`--yes/-y`: Skip confirmation.

### reject[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#reject "Direct link to reject")

Reject pending changes to one or more project files.

```
plandex reject file.ts # one fileplandex reject file.ts another-file.ts # multiple filesplandex reject --all # all pending filespdx rj file.ts # alias
```

`--all/-a`: Reject all pending files.

History[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#history "Direct link to History")
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### log[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#log "Direct link to log")

Show plan history.

```
plandex logplandex history # aliasplandex logs # alias
```

### rewind[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#rewind "Direct link to rewind")

Rewind to a previous state.

```
plandex rewind # rewind 1 stepplandex rewind 3 # rewind 3 stepsplandex rewind a7c8d66 # rewind to a specific step from `plandex log`
```

With no arguments, Plandex rewinds one step.

With one argument, Plandex rewinds the specified number of steps (if an integer is passed) or rewinds to the specified step (if a hash from `plandex log` is passed).

### convo[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#convo "Direct link to convo")

Show the current plan's conversation.

```
plandex convoplandex convo 1 # show a specific messageplandex convo 1-5 # show a range of messagesplandex convo 3- # show all messages from 3 to the end
```

`--plain/-p`: Output conversation in plain text with no ANSI codes.

### summary[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#summary "Direct link to summary")

Show the latest summary of the current plan.

`--plain/-p`: Output summary in plain text with no ANSI codes.

Branches[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#branches "Direct link to Branches")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### branches[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#branches-1 "Direct link to branches")

List plan branches. Output includes index, name, when the branch was last updated, the number of tokens in context, and the number of tokens in the conversation (prior to summarization).

```
plandex branchespdx br # alias
```

### checkout[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#checkout "Direct link to checkout")

Checkout or create a branch.

```
plandex checkout # select from a list of branches or prompt to create a new branchplandex checkout some-branch # checkout by name or create a new branch with that namepdx co # alias
```

### delete-branch[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#delete-branch "Direct link to delete-branch")

Delete a branch by name or index.

```
plandex delete-branch # select from a list of branchesplandex delete-branch some-branch # by nameplandex delete-branch 4 # by index in `plandex branches`pdx db # alias
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of branches to select from.

With one argument, Plandex deletes a branch by name or by index in the `plandex branches` list.

Background Tasks / Streams[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#background-tasks--streams "Direct link to Background Tasks / Streams")
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ps[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#ps "Direct link to ps")

List active and recently finished plan streams. Output includes stream ID, plan name, branch name, when the stream was started, and the stream's status (active, finished, stopped, errored, or waiting for a missing file to be selected).

### connect[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#connect "Direct link to connect")

Connect to an active plan stream.

```
plandex connect # select from a list of active streamsplandex connect a4de # by stream ID in `plandex ps`plandex connect some-plan main # by plan name and branch name
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of active streams to select from.

With one argument, Plandex connects to a stream by stream ID in the `plandex ps` list.

With two arguments, Plandex connects to a stream by plan name and branch name.

### stop[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#stop "Direct link to stop")

Stop an active plan stream.

```
plandex stop # select from a list of active streamsplandex stop a4de # by stream ID in `plandex ps`plandex stop some-plan main # by plan name and branch name
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of active streams to select from.

With one argument, Plandex connects to a stream by stream ID in the `plandex ps` list.

With two arguments, Plandex connects to a stream by plan name and branch name.

Models[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models "Direct link to Models")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### models[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-1 "Direct link to models")

Show current plan models and model settings.

### models default[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-default "Direct link to models default")

Show org-wide default models and model settings for new plans.

### models available[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-available "Direct link to models available")

Show available models.

```
plandex models available # show all available modelsplandex models available --custom # show available custom models only
```

`--custom`: Show available custom models only.

### set-model[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#set-model "Direct link to set-model")

Update current plan models or model settings.

```
plandex set-model # select from a list of models and settingsplandex set-model planner openai/gpt-4 # set the model for a roleplandex set-model gpt-4-turbo-latest # set the current plan's model pack by name (sets all model roles at once—see `model-packs` below)plandex set-model builder temperature 0.1 # set a model setting for a roleplandex set-model max-tokens 4000 # set the planner model overall token limit to 4000plandex set-model max-convo-tokens 20000  # set how large the conversation can grow before Plandex starts using summaries
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you to select from a list of models and settings.

With arguments, can take one of the following forms:

*   `plandex set-model [role] [model]`: Set the model for a role.
*   `plandex set-model [model-pack]`: Set the current plan's model pack by name.
*   `plandex set-model [role] [setting] [value]`: Set a model setting for a role.
*   `plandex set-model [setting] [value]`: Set a model setting for the current plan.

Models are specified as `provider/model-name`, e.g. `openai/gpt-4`, `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-3`, `together/mistralai/Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct-v0.1`, etc.

See all the model roles [here](https://docs.plandex.ai/models/roles).

Model role settings:

*   `temperature`: Higher temperature means more randomness, which can produce more creativity but also more errors.
*   `top-p`: Top-p sampling is a way to prevent the model from generating improbable text by only considering the most likely tokens.

Plan settings:

*   `max-tokens`: The overall token limit for the planner model.
*   `max-convo-tokens`: How large the conversation can grow before Plandex starts using summaries.
*   `reserved-output-tokens`: The number of tokens reserved for output from the model.

### set-model default[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#set-model-default "Direct link to set-model default")

Update org-wide default model settings for new plans.

```
plandex set-model default # select from a list of models and settingsplandex set-model default planner openai/gpt-4 # set the model for a role# etc. — same options as `set-model` above
```

Works exactly the same as `set-model` above, but sets the default model settings for all new plans instead of only the current plan.

### models add[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-add "Direct link to models add")

Add a custom model.

Plandex will prompt you for all required information to add a custom model.

### models delete[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-delete "Direct link to models delete")

Delete a custom model.

```
plandex models delete # select from a list of custom modelsplandex models delete some-model # by nameplandex models delete 4 # by index in `plandex models available --custom`
```

### model-packs[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#model-packs "Direct link to model-packs")

Show all available model packs.

### model-packs create[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#model-packs-create "Direct link to model-packs create")

Create a new custom model pack.

```
plandex model-packs create
```

Plandex will prompt you for all required information to create a custom model pack.

### model-packs delete[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#model-packs-delete "Direct link to model-packs delete")

Delete a custom model pack.

```
plandex model-packs deleteplandex model-packs delete some-model-pack # by nameplandex model-packs delete 4 # by index in `plandex model-packs --custom`
```

Account Management[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#account-management "Direct link to Account Management")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### sign-in[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#sign-in "Direct link to sign-in")

Sign in, accept an invite, or create an account.

Plandex will prompt you for all required information to sign in, accept an invite, or create an account.

### invite[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#invite "Direct link to invite")

Invite a user to join your org.

```
plandex invite # prompt for email, name, and roleplandex invite name@domain.com 'Full Name' member # invite with email, name, and role 
```

Users can be invited as `member`, `admin`, or `owner`.

### revoke[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#revoke "Direct link to revoke")

Revoke an invite or remove a user from your org.

```
plandex revoke # select from a list of users and invitesplandex revoke name@domain.com # by email
```

### users[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#users "Direct link to users")

List users and pending invites in your org.
generate commands for code base summary

Here are some potential commands for generating a summary of a code base:
```
# Generate a summary of the current plan's code base
plandex summary code-base

# Generate a summary of a specific branch's code base
plandex summary code-base --branch some-branch

# Generate a summary of the code base in plain text format
plandex summary code-base --plain

# Generate a detailed summary of the code base, including file names and sizes
plandex summary code-base --detailed

# Generate a summary of a specific directory in the code base
plandex summary code-base /path/to/directory

# Generate a summary of the code base, excluding certain files or directories
plandex summary code-base --exclude /path/to/exclude1 /path/to/exclude2
```

These commands would provide different options for generating a summary of a code base, including the ability to specify a branch, output format (plain text or ANSI codes), level of detail, specific directories, and excluded files or directories.

### log[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#log "Direct link to log")

Show plan history.

```
plandex logplandex history # aliasplandex logs # alias
```

### rewind[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#rewind "Direct link to rewind")

Rewind to a previous state.

```
plandex rewind # rewind 1 stepplandex rewind 3 # rewind 3 stepsplandex rewind a7c8d66 # rewind to a specific step from `plandex log`
```

With no arguments, Plandex rewinds one step.

With one argument, Plandex rewinds the specified number of steps (if an integer is passed) or rewinds to the specified step (if a hash from `plandex log` is passed).

### convo[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#convo "Direct link to convo")

Show the current plan's conversation.

```
plandex convoplandex convo 1 # show a specific messageplandex convo 1-5 # show a range of messagesplandex convo 3- # show all messages from 3 to the end
```

`--plain/-p`: Output conversation in plain text with no ANSI codes.

### summary[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#summary "Direct link to summary")

Show the latest summary of the current plan.

`--plain/-p`: Output summary in plain text with no ANSI codes.

Branches[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#branches "Direct link to Branches")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### branches[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#branches-1 "Direct link to branches")

List plan branches. Output includes index, name, when the branch was last updated, the number of tokens in context, and the number of tokens in the conversation (prior to summarization).

```
plandex branchespdx br # alias
```

### checkout[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#checkout "Direct link to checkout")

Checkout or create a branch.

```
plandex checkout # select from a list of branches or prompt to create a new branchplandex checkout some-branch # checkout by name or create a new branch with that namepdx co # alias
```

### delete-branch[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#delete-branch "Direct link to delete-branch")

Delete a branch by name or index.

```
plandex delete-branch # select from a list of branchesplandex delete-branch some-branch # by nameplandex delete-branch 4 # by index in `plandex branches`pdx db # alias
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of branches to select from.

With one argument, Plandex deletes a branch by name or by index in the `plandex branches` list.

Background Tasks / Streams[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#background-tasks--streams "Direct link to Background Tasks / Streams")
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ps[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#ps "Direct link to ps")

List active and recently finished plan streams. Output includes stream ID, plan name, branch name, when the stream was started, and the stream's status (active, finished, stopped, errored, or waiting for a missing file to be selected).

### connect[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#connect "Direct link to connect")

Connect to an active plan stream.

```
plandex connect # select from a list of active streamsplandex connect a4de # by stream ID in `plandex ps`plandex connect some-plan main # by plan name and branch name
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of active streams to select from.

With one argument, Plandex connects to a stream by stream ID in the `plandex ps` list.

With two arguments, Plandex connects to a stream by plan name and branch name.

### stop[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#stop "Direct link to stop")

Stop an active plan stream.

```
plandex stop # select from a list of active streamsplandex stop a4de # by stream ID in `plandex ps`plandex stop some-plan main # by plan name and branch name
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you with a list of active streams to select from.

With one argument, Plandex connects to a stream by stream ID in the `plandex ps` list.

With two arguments, Plandex connects to a stream by plan name and branch name.

Models[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models "Direct link to Models")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### models[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-1 "Direct link to models")

Show current plan models and model settings.

### models default[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-default "Direct link to models default")

Show org-wide default models and model settings for new plans.

### models available[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#models-available "Direct link to models available")

Show available models.

```
plandex models available # show all available modelsplandex models available --custom # show available custom models only
```

`--custom`: Show available custom models only.

### set-model[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#set-model "Direct link to set-model")

Update current plan models or model settings.

```
plandex set-model # select from a list of models and settingsplandex set-model planner openai/gpt-4 # set the model for a roleplandex set-model gpt-4-turbo-latest # set the current plan's model pack by name (sets all model roles at once—see `model-packs` below)plandex set-model builder temperature 0.1 # set a model setting for a roleplandex set-model max-tokens 4000 # set the planner model overall token limit to 4000plandex set-model max-convo-tokens 20000  # set how large the conversation can grow before Plandex starts using summaries
```

With no arguments, Plandex prompts you to select from a list of models and settings.

With arguments, can take one of the following forms:

*   `plandex set-model [role] [model]`: Set the model for a role.
*   `plandex set-model [model-pack]`: Set the current plan's model pack by name.
*   `plandex set-model [role] [setting] [value]`: Set a model setting for a role.
*   `plandex set-model [setting] [value]`: Set a model setting for the current plan.

Models are specified as `provider/model-name`, e.g. `openai/gpt-4`, `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-3`, `together/mistralai/Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct-v0.1`, etc.

See all the model roles [here](https://docs.plandex.ai/models/roles).

Model role settings:

*   `temperature`: Higher temperature means more randomness, which can produce more creativity but also more errors.
*   `top-p`: Top-p sampling is a way to prevent the model from generating improbable text by only considering the most likely tokens.

Plan settings:

*   `max-tokens`: The overall token limit for the planner model.
*   `max-convo-tokens`: How large the conversation can grow before Plandex starts using summaries.
*   `reserved-output-tokens`: The number of tokens reserved for output from the model.

### set-model default[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#set-model-default "Direct link to set-model default")

Update org-wide default model settings for new plans.

```
plandex set-model default # select from a list of models and settingsplandex set-model default planner openai/gpt-4 # set the model for a role# etc. — same options as `set-model` above
```

Works exactly the same as `set-model` above, but sets the default model settings for all new plans instead of only the current plan.

Account Management[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#account-management "Direct link to Account Management")
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### sign-in[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#sign-in "Direct link to sign-in")

Sign in, accept an invite, or create an account.

Plandex will prompt you for all required information to sign in, accept an invite, or create an account.

### invite[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#invite "Direct link to invite")

Invite a user to join your org.

```
plandex invite # prompt for email, name, and roleplandex invite name@domain.com 'Full Name' member # invite with email, name, and role 
```

Users can be invited as `member`, `admin`, or `owner`.

### revoke[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#revoke "Direct link to revoke")

Revoke an invite or remove a user from your org.

```
plandex revoke # select from a list of users and invitesplandex revoke name@domain.com # by email
```

### users[​](https://docs.plandex.ai/cli-reference#users "Direct link to users")

List users and pending invites in your org.
